signal.title: JARVIS: An Agent That Designs, Builds, and Tests Circuit Boards on Its Own
signal.summary: 这项研究聚焦机器人操作任务，尝试把感知、语言理解和动作控制连接起来，完成更稳定的抓取或操作。

editorial.intro: 这项研究聚焦机器人操作任务，尝试把感知、语言理解和动作控制连接起来，完成更稳定的抓取或操作。
editorial.why_it_matters: 灵巧操作是具身智能最接近真实生产和服务场景的能力，也是检验模型泛化和控制可靠性的直接环节。
editorial.watch_next: 继续核对物体变化、未见场景和长序列操作中的成功率。

evidence.title: JARVIS: An Agent That Designs, Builds, and Tests Circuit Boards on Its Own
evidence.excerpt: Power electronics is central to the energy transition, but developing new hardware still relies on human-led design, fabrication, testing, and iteration. We present JARVIS, an embodied AI agent that autonomously closes this loop for circuit boards. JARVIS maintains machine-specific capabilities and constraints, scans its workspace using a robot-mounted 3D scanner, and constructs an executable digital twin in which it rehearses robot motions, fabrication steps, and circuit behavior before consuming materials. A single text instruction initiates the physical experiment. Using unmodified desktop equipment, the agent coordinates a robot arm, a PCB printer that deposits conductive silver ink and solder paste, and a pick-and-place machine. It verifies progress using cameras and sensors, then tests the fabricated circuit with an OPAL-RT real-time simulator and an oscilloscope. Based on the measurements, JARVIS diagnoses deviations from the design and generates a revised design in KiCad for subsequent rehearsal.
